themes_detail.label: Dead trees spike this week
themes_detail.summary: Dead or dying tree complaints surged to 8 reports THIS WEEK, up 357% from the 1.8-complaint weekly average over the prior 8 weeks, suggesting either a recent disease outbreak, storm damage, or sudden failure of multiple trees across CD 501.
evidence: 8 dead/dying tree complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.8 weekly average (z-score: 5.21)
357% spike represents most recent statistically significant anomaly in dataset
Companion spike in Illegal Tree Damage (5 complaints 2 weeks ago, +264%) suggests possible concurrent tree health crisis
reporting_angles: Investigate whether a specific disease, pest, or weather event triggered tree failures across the district
Interview Parks Department about tree maintenance backlogs and whether Staten Island's aging tree inventory is at risk

themes_detail.label: Lot conditions deteriorating
themes_detail.summary: Vacant lot condition complaints hit 3 reports THIS WEEK, an 1100% spike from the 0.2-complaint weekly baseline, indicating rapid degradation of outdoor spaces that may signal neglect, illegal dumping, or property abandonment.
evidence: 3 lot condition complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.2 weekly average (z-score: 4.16)
1100% spike is among the sharpest increases in current dataset
Aligns with ongoing community board requests for building code enforcement and illegal use prevention
reporting_angles: Map the 3 reported lots to determine if they're clustered in a specific neighborhood and what ownership pattern emerges
Examine whether lots are tied to active ULURP applications (5 development proposals in pipeline) or long-abandoned properties

themes_detail.label: Street-level vendor enforcement surge
themes_detail.summary: Vendor enforcement complaints exploded to 4 reports 3 weeks ago, a 3100% spike from the 0.1 weekly average, the highest percentage increase in the dataset and suggesting either aggressive enforcement action by the city or a sudden proliferation of unpermitted street vending.
evidence: 4 vendor enforcement complaints 3 WEEKS AGO vs. 0.1 weekly average (z-score: 11.72) — highest z-score in dataset
3100% spike indicates extreme departure from baseline, though now 2+ weeks old
Suggests either coordinated enforcement sweep or influx of street vendors in district
reporting_angles: Obtain NYPD and Department of Consumer Affairs enforcement records for CD 501 in past 4 weeks to determine if sweep occurred
Interview affected vendors and community members to determine if this was coordinated enforcement or organic vendor increase

themes_detail.label: Park rules violations spike
themes_detail.summary: Park rules violations reached 4 complaints LAST WEEK, a 1500% spike from the 0.2 weekly average, pointing to either enforcement crackdowns at public spaces or new disruptive behavior patterns at St. George or other district parks.
evidence: 4 park rules violation complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.2 weekly average (z-score: 8.66)
1500% spike is second-highest percentage increase in current dataset
Liotti Ikefugi Playground Reconstruction in public review phase may indicate broader park management changes
reporting_angles: Identify which parks generated violations and what specific infractions were cited (alcohol, crowds, hours, etc.)
Connect to recent playground reconstruction proposal to assess whether enforcement or infrastructure changes are driving complaints

themes_detail.label: For-hire vehicle complaints surge
themes_detail.summary: For-hire vehicle complaints jumped to 6 reports LAST WEEK, a 300% spike from the 1.5 weekly average, suggesting either increased Uber/Lyft presence, illegal parking by rideshare drivers, or increased resident complaints about traffic impacts.
evidence: 6 for-hire vehicle complaints LAST WEEK vs. 1.5 weekly average (z-score: 4.5)
300% increase mirrors broader concerns about rideshare congestion in outer boroughs
May overlap with illegal parking spike (1752 complaints over 90 days), suggesting driveway blocking or loading zone conflicts
reporting_angles: Analyze whether for-hire complaints cluster around specific transit hubs or residential areas
Interview residents and TLC about whether rideshare density has noticeably increased in St. George/Stapleton in past month
